correctness.rationale: At weight ≤5 one color covers at most ten vertices by open neighborhoods but at least eleven are blank. At weight six a class of two covers at most eight blanks: nonadjacent members have two common neighbors, while adjacent members occur in their own union of open neighborhoods. A smaller class covers at most five. Thus both classes are triples. Closed neighborhoods of distinct vertices intersect in two vertices; triple inclusion–exclusion and the two transitive triple types yield antineighborhood size three for independent and path triples and four for one-edge triples. A vertex outside N[A] must bear the other color, so the equality case forces B=F(A); the representative XOR computations and the transitivity of translations and direction permutations give F(B)=A, switching the two types. This proves feasibility and the disjoint, named-color classification. A one-copy move would keep one entire class fixed and is impossible. A fresh exhaustive audit included overlapping supports through weight six; it found 320 optima, 1,440 exact two-copy edges, degree nine, no triangles, and the common shell tuple (1,9,54,159,90,7) from all 320 starts, giving radius and diameter five.
